en: Well, don't be rude about it.
It's especially popular right now. This season's pennant race has definitely been the most exciting, compared to the past few years.
Yeah, I've noticed. When we win, a whole buncha folks will come here in a real good mood and ready t'drink the night away.
You're not a baseball fan yourself?
I don't know the rules, so even if I catch it when it's on TV, I don't have a clue what's goin' on.
Lately, I've come to realize people here in Hakata are much more intriguing than other places I've been.
Huh? Whatcha mean by intriguing?
When I first came to town, I thought the men here were pretty rough and unfriendly, but I've realized that's not the case.
Hehe, yeah. A lot of guys 'round here are kinda shy. It can be easy to mistake that for being snobbish, but folks are actually real nice.
Once ya spend enough time talkin' to them, most are friendly enough.
So it seems. Recently, I've come to understand that more.
That's a hassle, though. I'd rather people were straight-up from the start.
That's what makes people intriguing, I guess.
Hm. That's one way of putting it, I suppose.
But come to think of it, you're kinda like us Hakata folk, Kiryu-san.
Maybe so. My coming here wasn't really part of the plan, but I think this town suits me.
Yeah! Shy at first, but actually real nice and kindhearted when folks get to know ya. I'd say that describes you, right?
Yeah, I suppose...
Right. You bein' a sort of Hakata person must be why we get along so well!
Very true. I never would've expected I'd get on so well with a Hakata girl.
I always thought Hakata girls were meant for Hakata guys, but guess I gotta rethink that some.
Hm? Did you say something?
No, no, it's nothin'!
I'm not from Hakata.
Well, no, but you do live here, so that makes ya Hakata folk in my book.
Sure, but...
Hey, it's all about what's in your heart! If y'love it here in Hakata, you're one of us.
Heh. I guess that's just the way people here think.
I'm just me. How I feel about things isn't necessarily because I have a Hakata mindset.
Well, yeah, but...
I don't want to be judged for whether or not I'm like a Hakata native. I want to be seen as an individual.
But you're the one who was just sayin' how folks in Hakata are nice!
How come you're so against bein' seen as one of us, anyway? That's weird!
I guess you have a point. Sorry about that.
Is it just me, or are there a lot of really pretty women in Fukuoka?
Really? I think it might just be you.
It's really just me?
You're pretty.
Oh, stop it. I know what you did there.
Maybe you're just an exception.
Awwww, stop, you! Flattery won't get ya anywhere, mister!
It's not just me. I've been all over, so I wouldn't say it unless it was true.
Is that so? I woulda figured the girls out in Tokyo were way cuter.
Maybe the folks in this part of town are just the best Fukuoka has to offer.
Fancy, good-lookin' girls from all over Fukuoka⑬heck, from all over Kyushu⑬might all just tend t'gather here.
I see. Even so, that still means there are a lot of good-looking women around here, right?
Yeah, but that's only a small part of it.
I've heard this part of the country is known for having lots of attractive ladies, though. I wonder why?
Hm. I do wonder...
That's not it. By that logic, cities like Tokyo and Osaka would have more pretty girls, too.
Oh, that's true.
So, I'd still say there are more than the usual amount of pretty girls in Fukuoka to begin with.
Wow, really?
Really.

en: Hmm. But I ain't all that pretty.
Well, I'm looking at you as an example.
If you travel a bit outside the city, I'm sure you'll find a buncha normal lookin' girls.
Whaaat? Hey, you're the one who brought the topic up, Kiryu-san!
On second thought, it's really nothing to get so worked up over.
Hahaha! Oh, you're so silly, Kiryu-san.
Hey, do you like spicy fish roe?
Of course! I always chow down on it with rice!
Apparently, it's good for your looks.
Yeah. It's loaded with vitamin E, which is good for your skin, and it also slows down the aging process.
Neat!
Also, the capsaicin in the chili peppers breaks down fatty acids, and it contains more probiotics than yogurt.
Wow, really? I've been eatin' it all this time and not knowing any of this.
Heh. Maybe that's why your skin is so smooth.
Haha! All thanks to spicy fish roe, huh?
I don't like tonkotsu, but I'm a big fan of spicy fish roe! I'm glad I was born in Hakata!
Haha.
Hey, I should pick some up on the way home! I've got a sudden cravin' for it now!
Just don't buy too much, now.
When I open my Western restaurant, maybe I'll have dishes with spicy fish roe in 'em!
Oh, that's not a bad idea.
Aha, I know! I'll try adding some spicy fish roe to the recipes for stuff I already make!
Are you sure that's a good idea?
Kiryu-san, you mentioned this before.
Huh? Did I?
You must be really interested in this topic.
Have you heard about tomato tonkotsu ramen? Apparently, it's easier to eat for those who are put off by the smell of the broth.
No, I haven't. What is it?
It's topped with tomato and basil, which helps to cut the richness of the tonkotsu broth.
Oooh, hey, I mighta heard of that! Someone called it a crime against tonkotsu. Does it taste good?
Apparently the flavor is sort of Italian, but even people who are put off by the scent of tonkotsu can enjoy it.
Huh. I'll have to try it sometime!
Kiryu-san, do you ever eat rice with your ramen?
Sometimes... But I'm not going to put rice on my face.
Hahahahaha!
If the tonkotsu doesn't smell too much, then I think I should be able to eat it.
I think you'll be fine.
When I open my restaurant, hopefully I can come up with dishes that lotsa folks can enjoy.
That's definitely worth considering.
My restaurant is gonna have an all-original, totally unique menu! I ain't gonna get beat by my competitors! No way!
Well, do your best.
Did you know chicken mizutaki is full of collagen? It's supposed to be good for you.
Oh wow, is that so?
Don't you eat it often? It's a Hakata specialty, right?
Well, it's kind of a pain to make. Everyone has their own schedule for meals at home, so we don't really eat it there.
But there's a pretty famous restaurant nearby, so when I do eat it, it's usually there.
It's way better at a restaurant, anyways. Hey, maybe you can have some rice with it, too, huh?
You won't let that go, will you?
The smell of mizutaki's way better than tonkotsu! If the food stalls all sold mizutaki instead, that'd be A-OK with me!
You really hate tonkotsu that much?
Since I wanna open a Western-style restaurant, mizutaki's not all that interesting to me.
Yeah, it definitely doesn't fit the theme.
But after I get married, I'd love to sit around the hotpot, eatin' with my husband and my kids at home.
That's much more homey than curry, yeah.
Apparently, there's a vending machine near here that's the only one of its kind in Japan.
Oh yeah, I saw that on TV! Where is it?
I don't know where, exactly.
Whaaat? I wanted to know what it shoots out.
Anyhow, it's wicked cool how folks come from all over to see it! Like, they come to Fukuoka just to buy juice from the machine.
I'd like to see it myself at some point.
When I open my restaurant, I don't wanna be just number one, I wanna be the only one! I want it to be loved by everyone!
Yeah, that'd be nice.
Speaking of, I took a road trip recently to buy somethin' that wasn't available locally.
Oh? What did you go buy?
It was a cake. But then after I got it, I found out you can just order it online. That just took the wind right outta my sails.
That's kind of a shame.
There's lotsa stuff in Japan you can only get in one particular place. I want my restaurant to be like that too.
Just don't make anything too weird.
I hear Hakata textiles are popular with women nowadays.
Oh yeah, they're wicked pretty! One of the other girls here at the club got a wallet as a present from one of her clients.
They make wallets? I assumed it was all just stuff like kimonos and sashes.
Nah, they even make shoes, too.
Oh, wow.
I'll have a pair of shoes, then!
I never said I was entertaining requests. Geez.
But we talked about how I gotta rein in my shopping, didn't we?
Hm. I'll think about it.
Speaking of which...
I don't think I've ever gotten a present from someone I've been dating.
But you're popular with the guys, aren't you?
I'm great at cooking, and okay at sewing. I wonder if I'd be able to weave together a kimono or somethin'.
That seems a bit unrealistic.
I just wish I could make something like that.
So, what kind of things do you like?
Huh? Well, what sorta things do ya mean?
What kind of food do you like?
Gotta be potatoes!
That was a quick answer.
I can't resist the texture of a hot potato! And they're even supposed to be good for you!
Really? I'd figure it'd be the other way around.
Nope! They're good for your skin and can clear up swelling and constipation. Plus, they're way lower in calories than y'might think!
Aw, just talkin' about them is making me wanna go out and eat 'em! Kiryu-san, would ya treat me to some one day?
Heh, sure thing.
Is there anything that you want?
What? Are you getting me a present?
No... I just want to know.
Let's see. Y'know, anything's fine by me, really.
Are you just saying that?
No, really. I just mean like, I'm not all that into brand-name stuff, y'know?
If I get somethin' wicked expensive, I kinda feel guilty about it and all.
Ah, okay. I get what you mean now.
What do you like about your job? Why are you working here?
Hm. Well, to earn money.
But it's not an easy job.
Well, sometimes it can be kinda rough, yeah. But I guess that goes for any job, right?
Plus, I like talkin' to folks. Having the chance to chat up so many people is right up my alley.
I guess it's more fun than I'd thought.
What are your hobbies?
Hobbies, huh? Well, lately, I've been wicked busy, so I stay at home a lot.
What do you do at home?
I've been readin' an awful lot lately.
Really? What sort of things do you read?
Lately, it's been mysteries. Stuff that's been turned into TV miniseries. Do you do much readin', Kiryu-san?
A bit here and there.
Oh yeah? What sorta books do y'read?
Well, given how busy I am with work lately, it's mostly been business manuals and the like.
Gotta keep your studies up to snuff, huh? So ya haven't read books for pleasure then?
Not lately, no. I've fallen behind on my current events and magazine reading.
Aww. There are lotsa really good books out there. You oughta try and read more.
You're right. I should pick something up.
Not much, no. When I have time away from work, I mostly read the newspaper.
See, I'm the opposite. I ain't never read the paper.
How do you stay up on current events, then? Isn't having conversation topics at hand a big part of a hostess' job?
I just get all the news on my phone. Readin' the newspaper's a big hassle, 'cause it seems totally disorganized.
I guess you're a sign of the times.
What do you do when you're out of the house?
Oh, I'm really into swimming and stuff.
I like to swim, too. I used to live in Okinawa, after all.
Really!? Oh, I'm wicked jealous! I bet the ocean must be real pretty there!
Yeah. Words really don't do it justice.
That sounds nice. I'd like to go there someday.
Maybe we can go together, just you and me.
Y'mean it? Because I'd totally go!
All right. It's a deal.
What are your thoughts when it comes to romance?
Romance? Like, in what sense?
What do you look for in a man?
What do I look for? Hmm. Nothin' specific, really.
That can't be true. You must have some standards, whether it's education, income, or even height.
Like not wantin' someone with a part-time job?
Yeah, that sort of thing.
Hmm. Well, when I like someone, I just kinda get a feeling. Outta the blue, I just sorta think, "Yeah, he's nice."
Then I guess there's no way for a guy to gain an advantage with you...
Are you okay with cheating?
Hmm. Yeah, I guess I'd probably let it slide.
Oh, really? Why's that?
Well, if I really like someone, I don't wanna split up with them right then and there, even if they cheat on me.
Why do y'ask, Kiryu-san? Do you cheat?
What if I said yes? What would you do?
Well, I'd be more at ease with ya comin' out with it than keeping it a secret.
I see. I understand how you think.
So, now that you know, what are ya gonna do? You planning on switchin' to another hostess?
